### Describe the bug

## Description:
(the full traceback is in the bottom to not make this part messy)
When trying to run a default GPT-OSS code for inference, the execution fails depending on the length of initial prompt. If the prompt only takes <=519 tokens, it runs successfully. If it's at least 520 tokens long - I get an assertion error in file `triton_kernels/matmul_ogs_details/opt_flags.py` in this chunck of code:
```python
    num_stages = -1
    for ep in subtiles_to_check:
        ns = opt_flags_nvidia.compute_num_stages(*compute_num_stages_args, ep, epilogue_effective_itemsize)
        if ns > num_stages:
            epilogue_subtile, num_stages = ep, ns
    assert num_stages >= 1
    if constraints.get("num_stages", None):
        num_stages = constraints["num_stages"]
```
Here, `num_stages` is 0, and so the assertion fails. However, simply forcing `num_stages` and `epilogue_subtile` be equal to 1 fixes the issue. It looks like this assertions can be avoided, yet still produce results

I don't have enough knowledge to understand, why is this assertion needed or what those variables even mean, so I am sorry in advance for not providing any insights. If this will not lead to any changes in the code, at least maybe some people can use the same temporary fix as me :) Speaking of, ...


## Temporary fix:
- go to your .cache folder, find triton_kernels in huggingface/hub and open file triton_kernels/matmul_ogs_details/opt_flags.py
  (for example, in my case, `/root/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--kernels-community--triton_kernels/snapshots/22b535b359d6c144e0152060dc6fec78da07039e/build/torch-universal/triton_kernels/matmul_ogs_details/opt_flags.py`)
- go to line ~220, find the line `assert num_stages >= 1` and replace it with "num_stages, epilogue_subtile = 1, 1"


## How to reproduce:
### Warning: this will require ~30GB of network traffic and space on your drive
Create a conda environment file `environment.llm.yaml`:
```yaml
name: asr_llm
channels:
  - pytorch
  - nvidia
  - conda-forge
  - defaults
dependencies:
  - python==3.12
  - pip
  - pytorch-gpu
  - pytorch-cuda
  - pip:
    - --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128
    - torch
    - transformers==4.55.2
    - accelerate==1.10.0
    - triton>=3.4.0
    - kernels==0.9.0
    - python-multipart==0.0.20
    - bitsandbytes==0.46.1
    - git+https://github.com/triton-lang/triton.git@main#subdirectory=python/triton_kernels
    - transformers==4.55.2
```
And create this conda environment:
```bash
conda env create --name asr_llm --file=environment.llm.yaml
conda activate asr_llm
```
Create a main.py file for running simple prompt using transformers and gpt-oss:
```python
text = "Hello " * 4000
MAX_TOKENS = 520


import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

model_id = "openai/gpt-oss-20b"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    model_id,
    device_map="auto",
    torch_dtype="auto",
)

inputs = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt").to("cuda")
print("Original shape:", inputs["input_ids"].shape)
inputs["input_ids"] = inputs["input_ids"][:, :MAX_TOKENS]

model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=10)
```
Now run this code `python main.py`
If `MAX_LENGTH` is set to 520 or bigger, it will cause an error. If less, than no error will be raised
